verdict.line: You lose the poke phase and risk a true-damage execute from Feast before level 6, but the matchup evens out once you can close distance and start contesting skirmishes with your knockup.

brief.thesis: Cho'Gath's Rupture (950 range) outranges every tool you have to initiate, so he can poke you down from distance while Vorpal Spikes adds free damage on top of any auto trade you take back. That ranged pressure, plus a true-damage Feast coming online at 6, is why this matchup sits at 45.2% over 310 games despite Malphite's overall 52% win rate in top lane. You don't out-poke Cho'Gath here — you survive the poke phase and look for all-in windows when his Q is down.

theirWindow.what: Feast deals a high amount of true damage and heals/grows him on a kill (max 6 stacks) — do not walk into melee range at low HP, since this is a straight execute, not a damage race.

yourWindow.what: With his 950-range poke down for 9 seconds, close with Q's movement-speed steal and commit your full E/W combo — this is the window where he can't kite you back out to max range.

start.why: The standard pick in this matchup (71.4% pick rate) — the extra potions buy you sustain through Cho'Gath's early Q/E poke without needing to recall.

boots.why: Tenacity cuts the duration of Feral Scream's silence and Rupture's slow, and the magic resist directly answers Cho'Gath's Q/W/R damage profile — the higher-winrate boots in this matchup (46.3%).

core.why: HP and sustained damage let you stand in range to threaten trades instead of just absorbing poke.
Punishes a champion that leans on auto-attacks to proc Vorpal Spikes, and the healing cut matters against his Carnivore sustain.
The magic shield blunts burst from Q/W plus a Feast true-damage hit, and this path has the best measured winrate (57.1% over 7 games) of the listed build paths.

runes.keystoneWhy: Free poke damage whenever he commits to a Rupture or Feral Scream attempt and misses the follow-up — this page carries the best measured winrate (47.3%) and Second Wind directly offsets his ranged poke.

summoners.why: The most-picked combo in this matchup (74.4% pick) — this is a defensive-shape lane overall, so Teleport lets you reset to full resources after being poked out rather than fighting from behind.

playing.title: Pop W before committing
playing.detail: Brutal Strikes boosts your Armor and Attack Damage for a short window, which also scales up your Armor-based E damage — activate it just before you plan to trade.

playing.title: Use Q to close, not poke
playing.detail: Seismic Shard (8s cooldown, 625 range) steals his movement speed — it's your only answer to Rupture's superior range, so use it to catch him, not from max distance.

playing.title: Walk off Rupture's reticle
playing.detail: It's a ground-targeted ability at 950 range, not a cone — side-stepping the cast location avoids the knockup and slow entirely.

playing.title: Stay outside Feral Scream's cone
playing.detail: At 300 range it silences you, shutting down your whole kit for its duration — don't walk into that range when you need Q or E to trade back.

playing.title: Time trades around Granite Shield
playing.detail: The passive shield only absorbs damage once it's had time to recharge since your last hit — check whether it's up before initiating.

playing.title: Respect Feast once he's 6
playing.detail: At 175 range, Feast deals a high amount of true damage and can outright execute you at low HP — don't commit to melee range under half health.

playing.title: Save R for skirmishes, not 1v1s
playing.detail: Unstoppable Force's cooldown runs 130 seconds at rank 1 down to 80 at rank 5 — missing it in a duel that doesn't kill wastes your best teamfight tool.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate figures above come from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1); the mechanical reasoning and trade-timing advice are my own tactical read on top of that data.
